messages.content: I want to settle transportation for Carlsbad now. We land at San Diego at 10:35 Thursday morning and fly home Monday at 1:40 p.m. Please price the whole thing door to door, including our outings to Torrey Pines on Friday and the San Diego Zoo on Saturday. I need to know whether keeping a rental car is actually worth it.

I’ll compare four-night airport rental, rideshares throughout, rail with local connections, and a one-day Carlsbad rental. One detail may materially change the result: your Tamarack confirmation says one self-parking space is included, although the earlier planning notes treated hotel parking as an extra charge. I’m going to verify that before totaling anything.
Yes, verify it directly against the reservation. I don’t want a cheap rental quote followed by four nights of parking charges.

Verified on confirmation TBR-618224: one standard self-parking space is included for all four nights. There is no nightly hotel parking charge for the reserved Partial Ocean View King. Oversize vehicles and a second vehicle would cost extra, so I’ll compare ordinary car classes only.
Good. What do the airport rental numbers look like with taxes, fees, fuel, and parking at the places we’re visiting?

The best current airport option is a midsize car from National: pickup at SAN Thursday at 11:30 a.m. and return Monday at 11:15 a.m. The rental is $284.16 total, including airport concession fees and taxes. Estimated fuel for the airport transfers plus both outings is $30. Torrey Pines charges $25 for the main reserve lot on Friday; San Diego Zoo parking is free, and Tamarack parking is included. Estimated trip transportation total: $339.16.
Check the counter hours against both flights. Also, is 11:15 early enough for a 1:40 departure?

National’s SAN facility is open from 4:30 a.m. to midnight on both Thursday and Monday, and returns operate throughout those hours. Your 10:35 a.m. arrival leaves ample time for the 11:30 pickup. Returning at 11:15 a.m. puts you at the terminal around 11:30 after the rental shuttle, about two hours ten minutes before departure. That is workable for a domestic flight. I would leave Tamarack around 10:25 to allow for traffic, refueling, and the return inspection.
Now compare that with rideshare for every leg. Use realistic totals, not the lowest fare that only appears when no one needs it.

Using scheduled-trip estimates and allowing for normal daytime variation: SAN to Tamarack is about $72 including tip, and Tamarack to SAN Monday morning about $84. The Torrey Pines round trip is approximately $76, and the zoo round trip approximately $110. That totals about $342, with a reasonable working range of $310 to $390 if demand changes. It avoids driving and parking, but the midpoint is essentially the same as the rental.
What about the train? Make sure it is actually running when we need it, especially Monday morning.

For Thursday, you can take a rideshare from SAN to Old Town Transit Center, then the northbound COASTER to Carlsbad Village and walk roughly ten minutes to Tamarack. The posted weekday schedule has departures after your arrival, including options around midday. On Monday, southbound morning trains from Carlsbad Village reach Old Town with enough time to transfer by rideshare and arrive at SAN before 11:30 a.m. for the 1:40 flight. The train is operating on both travel days, but a missed connection can add roughly an hour.
Give me the full transit total, including getting between the airport and Old Town and reaching both outings.

Airport-to-Old Town rideshares in both directions are about $36 total. COASTER fares for two adults on the airport-transfer legs total about $26. Torrey Pines is awkward from Carlsbad by transit, so a rideshare round trip is about $76. For the zoo, COASTER plus local MTS fares for two are about $38. The combined estimate is $176. That is the least expensive plan, but it involves luggage transfers on both flight days and about three hours of combined transit time for the zoo outing.
And the one-day local rental idea? Could we pick it up Saturday and use it for both Torrey Pines and the zoo without paying for a second day?

A Carlsbad Village branch has a Saturday midsize car from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. for $78.42 including taxes, with after-hours key return available. Estimated fuel is $15 and Torrey Pines parking is $25. Adding the $62 rail-and-airport-transfer plan gives $180.42 if you move both outings to Saturday. The drawback is the itinerary: Carlsbad to Torrey Pines, then across to the zoo, then back to Carlsbad makes for a long day and eliminates the separate Friday outing you planned.
No, I don’t want to combine them. Is there a hybrid that keeps Friday at Torrey Pines and Saturday at the zoo?

Yes. Use rail for both airport transfers, rent locally on Friday for Torrey Pines, and take COASTER plus MTS to the zoo Saturday. The estimate is $62 for the flight-day rail connections, $78.42 for the Friday rental, $15 fuel, $25 reserve parking, and $38 for Saturday transit. Total: $218.42. It saves about $121 compared with the airport rental, but adds two rail transfers with luggage and makes the zoo trip substantially longer than driving.
So the full rental is $339.16, rideshare is around $342, transit is $176, and the hybrid is $218.42. Is that all for both of us?

Correct. Each figure covers both travelers and all four required movements: arrival transfer, departure transfer, Friday at Torrey Pines, and Saturday at the zoo. The rental totals also include estimated fuel and the $25 Torrey Pines parking charge. Meals and optional stops are not included.
The airport rental sounds simplest, especially since the hotel parking is included. Before booking, tell me the cancellation terms and whether my wife can drive it too.

The National reservation is pay later, with no cancellation fee before the scheduled pickup time. A no-show is not charged because no prepayment is required. In California, a spouse may be added as an authorized driver without an additional-driver fee; both of you must present valid licenses at pickup. The $284.16 rate includes unlimited mileage but not fuel, tolls, optional insurance, or the Torrey Pines lot.
Book that midsize car in my name. Keep the pickup and return times you quoted, and don’t add insurance or prepaid fuel.

The midsize car is reserved with National for Avery Thompson. Pickup is at San Diego International Airport on Thursday, June 18 at 11:30 a.m.; return is Monday, June 22 at 11:15 a.m. Confirmation NAT-6184AV is pay later for $284.16 including taxes and airport fees, with unlimited mileage. No optional insurance or prepaid fuel was added. Your wife can be added at the counter at no fee after presenting her license. With estimated fuel and Torrey Pines parking, the working door-to-door transportation total is $339.16. Tamarack’s included parking remains verified, and the local rental and rideshare options were not reserved.
